David M. Solomon (born 1962) is an American investment banker who has served as chairman and chief executive officer of The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. since 2018. He succeeded Lloyd Blankfein in the role on October 1, 2018, becoming the first leader without prior experience as the firm's sole chief operating officer. Solomon is notable for his parallel pursuit of electronic dance music production and performance under the pseudonym D-Sol, an avocation he began in 2015 that has included releases charting on Billboard and appearances at events worldwide.

Within the firm, he advanced rapidly, co-heading the high-yield and leveraged loan business, joining the management committee in 2004, and serving as co-head of the investment banking division from 2006 to 2016. In 2017, he was named president and co-chief operating officer, assuming sole COO responsibilities in 2018 prior to his elevation to CEO.

Solomon holds additional leadership positions outside Goldman Sachs, including as chairman of the Hamilton College board of trustees and as a board member for the Robin Hood Foundation, NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital, and the Paley Center for Media. Before assuming his role as CEO, Solomon was president and chief operating officer (COO) from January 2017 to September 2018, and was joint head of the investment banking division from July 2006 to December 2016. Solomon formally succeeded Lloyd Blankfein, the previous CEO, on October 1, 2018, and was named chairman after Blankfein's retirement.

Solomon also recreationally creates electronic dance music (EDM). He has performed at nightclubs and music festivals around New York, Miami and The Bahamas.

Solomon was born in Hartsdale, New York to a Jewish family. His father, Alan Solomon, was an executive vice president of a small publishing company, and his mother, Sandra, worked as an audiology supervisor. Solomon attended Hamilton College in Clinton, New York, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science. While there, he played on the rugby team and was chairman of the college's Alpha Delta Phi chapter.

Solomon formally succeeded Lloyd Blankfein, the previous CEO, on October 1, 2018, and was named chairman after Blankfein's retirement.

# David Solomon Is Appointed CEO and Chairman
![profile-card](https://goldmansachs.com/images/migrated/our-firm/history/moments/150th-multimedia/2018-solomon-ceo/350x450.jpg)
After the retirement of Lloyd Blankfein in 2018, David Solomon is appointed CEO and chairman of Goldman Sachs.
In mid-2018, Goldman Sachs announced that as of September 30 of that year, [Lloyd Blankfein](https://goldmansachs.com/our-firm/history/moments/2006-blankfein-assumes-leadership) would step down as chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs after 12 years of service in those roles. David Solomon, then president and chief operating officer, would succeed Lloyd, becoming CEO in October 2018 and chairman in January 2019.

Over the years, David also served as global head of the firm’s Financing Group, which handles all capital markets and derivative products for the firm’s corporate clients. He was appointed to the [Management Committee](https://goldmansachs.com/our-firm/history/moments/1965-management-committee) in 2004 and, in 2006, was named co-head of the Investment Banking Division (IBD), a role he held for 10 years. David became Goldman Sachs’ president and co-chief operating officer in January of 2017 and sole COO in March 2018, before ultimately stepping into the CEO position in October of 2018 and that of chairman in January 2019.
